exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 1, Practice Set 1

questions.jp: 32ビットで表現できるビットパターンの個数は、24ビットで表現できる個数の何倍か。
questions.romaji: 32-bitto de hyougen dekiru bitto pataan no kosuu wa, 24-bitto de hyougen dekiru kosuu no nanbai ka.
questions.en: How many times as many bit patterns can be represented with 32 bits as with 24 bits?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Each extra bit doubles the number of patterns. Moving from 24 bits to 32 bits adds eight doubling steps, so the larger space has 256 times as many patterns.
Technical breakdown:
An n-bit value has 2^n possible bit patterns. The ratio is 2^32 / 2^24 = 2^(32-24) = 2^8 = 256.
Wrong answer analysis:
ア — 8 is the number of extra bits, but each extra bit doubles the count; the ratio is not the bit difference itself.
イ — 16 equals 2^4, so it accounts for only four of the eight extra bits.
ウ — 128 equals 2^7, which is one doubling short.
Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: 次の10進小数のうち、2進数で表すと無限小数になるものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Tsugi no juu-shin shousuu no uchi, ni-shinsuu de arawasu to mugen shousuu ni naru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which of the following decimal fractions becomes non-terminating when represented in binary?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Binary can finish cleanly only when a fraction can be built from halves, quarters, eighths, and other powers of two. The fraction 0.05 needs a factor of five, so its binary digits repeat forever.
Technical breakdown:
In lowest terms, a rational number terminates in base 2 only when its denominator is a power of 2. Here 0.05 = 1/20 and 20 = 2^2 × 5, so the factor 5 makes the binary expansion non-terminating.
Wrong answer analysis:
イ — 0.125 = 1/8 = 1/2^3, so it terminates in binary.
ウ — 0.375 = 3/8, whose reduced denominator is 2^3, so it terminates in binary.
エ — 0.5 = 1/2, so its binary form is exactly 0.1.
Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: 16進小数3A.5Cを10進数の分数で表したものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Juuroku-shin shousuu 3A.5C o juu-shinsuu no bunsuu de arawashita mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which of the following expresses the hexadecimal fraction 3A.5C as a base-10 fraction?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Hexadecimal places use powers of 16. Convert each place, add the values, then reduce the resulting fraction.
Technical breakdown:
3A.5C(hex) = 3×16 + 10 + 5/16 + 12/256 = 58 + 92/256 = 14940/256. Dividing numerator and denominator by 4 gives 3735/64.
Wrong answer analysis:
ア — 939/16 equals 58.6875, but 3A.5C equals 58.359375; the fractional hexadecimal places were combined incorrectly.
ウ — 14939/256 is one numerator unit below the unreduced value 14940/256.
エ — 14941/256 is one numerator unit above the unreduced value 14940/256.
Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 次の10進小数のうち、8進数に変換したときに有限小数になるものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Tsugi no juu-shin shousuu no uchi, hachi-shinsuu ni henkan shita toki ni yuugen shousuu ni naru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which of the following decimal fractions becomes a terminating fraction when converted to octal?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Octal is built from powers of two because 8 = 2^3. Fractions made only from halves can end cleanly in octal; 0.5 is exactly one half.
Technical breakdown:
A reduced fraction terminates in base 8 only when its denominator has no prime factors outside those of 8, so only factor 2 is allowed. 0.5 = 1/2 and therefore terminates.
Wrong answer analysis:
ア — 0.3 = 3/10, and denominator 10 contains factor 5, so its octal expansion repeats.
イ — 0.4 = 2/5, whose denominator contains factor 5, so it does not terminate in octal.
エ — 0.8 = 4/5, whose denominator contains factor 5, so it does not terminate in octal.
Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: 基数変換に関する記述のうち、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Kisuu henkan ni kansuru kijutsu no uchi, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement about radix/base conversion is correct?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 2進数の有限小数は、10進数にしても必ず有限小数になる。
options.romaji: Ni-shinsuu no yuugen shousuu wa, juu-shinsuu ni shite mo kanarazu yuugen shousuu ni naru.
options.en: A terminating binary fraction always remains terminating when converted to decimal.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 8進数の有限小数は、2進数にすると有限小数にならないこともある。
options.romaji: Hachi-shinsuu no yuugen shousuu wa, ni-shinsuu ni suru to yuugen shousuu ni naranai koto mo aru.
options.en: A terminating octal fraction may become non-terminating when converted to binary.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 8進数の有限小数は、10進数にすると有限小数にならないこともある。
options.romaji: Hachi-shinsuu no yuugen shousuu wa, juu-shinsuu ni suru to yuugen shousuu ni naranai koto mo aru.
options.en: A terminating octal fraction may become non-terminating when converted to decimal.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 10進数の有限小数は、8進数にしても必ず有限小数になる。
options.romaji: Juu-shinsuu no yuugen shousuu wa, hachi-shinsuu ni shite mo kanarazu yuugen shousuu ni naru.
options.en: A terminating decimal fraction always remains terminating when converted to octal.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A finite binary fraction is assembled from halves. Decimal notation can always write halves exactly, so a terminating binary fraction also terminates in decimal.
Technical breakdown:
A terminating binary fraction has a reduced denominator 2^n. Because 10^n = 2^n×5^n, multiplying by a suitable power of 5 expresses that value with a denominator that is a power of 10. Therefore its decimal expansion terminates.
Wrong answer analysis:
イ — One octal digit maps to exactly three binary digits, so every terminating octal fraction terminates in binary.
ウ — A terminating octal denominator is 8^n = 2^(3n); powers of two also produce terminating decimals.
エ — A terminating decimal may have factor 5 in its reduced denominator, as 0.1 = 1/10 does; base 8 has no factor 5, so such a value repeats in octal.
Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: 16進小数2A.4Cと等しいものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Juuroku-shin shousuu 2A.4C to hitoshii mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which of the following is equal to the hexadecimal fraction 2A.4C?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Turn each hexadecimal digit into four binary bits. The 1 bits tell us exactly which powers of two must be added.
Technical breakdown:
2A.4C(hex) = 0010 1010.0100 1100(binary). Left of the point, the set bits are at 2^5, 2^3, and 2^1. Right of the point, they are at 2^-2, 2^-5, and 2^-6.
Wrong answer analysis:
イ — Its fractional powers match binary .100110 rather than the required .01001100 positions; it incorrectly includes 2^-1, 2^-4, and 2^-5.
ウ — Its integer powers 2^6 + 2^4 + 2^2 describe hexadecimal 54 rather than 2A, although its fractional powers are correct.
エ — Both parts are wrong: the integer powers describe 54 and the fractional powers use the incorrect positions from option イ.
Correct answer: ア
